topic.title: Visual Robustness and Spurious Correlations
topic.overview: Visual models can succeed on familiar tests while relying on backgrounds, frequency patterns, or preprocessing choices that fail elsewhere. This topic investigates robustness to transformations, noise, and spurious correlations, alongside methods for revealing those dependencies. It treats benchmark design and architectural analysis as essential parts of understanding generalization.
topic.whyItMatters: Robustness is specific to the disturbance being tested. A model that resists one dataset’s shortcuts may still exploit shortcuts in its own training distribution, and improvements against Gaussian noise do not establish resistance to every distribution shift. Carefully targeted evaluations prevent overly broad claims.
topic.evolution: A 2015 method encourages locally isometric feature transformations to balance discrimination and robustness. Later work examines frequency sensitivity, invariance, and overinterpretation. CounterAnimal in 2024 exposes background dependence in CLIP models; a 2026 study analyzes how kernels, pooling, downsampling, and preprocessing influence robustness under explicitly defined Gaussian-noise protocols.
openQuestions: How can robustness benchmarks avoid inheriting the blind spots of their creators’ models?
Which architectural changes improve several forms of shift without sacrificing useful sensitivity?

papers.tldr: RaVL identifies misleading image-region associations and uses a region-aware training loss to improve vision-language model robustness.

papers.title: SELECT: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Data Curation Strategies for Image Classification
papers.tldr: SELECT compares image-dataset curation strategies at scale and finds that newer methods compete on some tasks while original ImageNet curation remains the reference standard.

papers.title: Semi-Truths: A Large-Scale Dataset of AI-Augmented Images for Evaluating Robustness of AI-Generated Image detectors
papers.tldr: Semi-Truths provides over 1.3 million locally AI-edited images to reveal how detector performance varies with edits, methods, and data distributions.

papers.title: The Unmet Promise of Synthetic Training Images: Using Retrieved Real Images Performs Better
papers.tldr: In the reported classification comparisons, retrieving relevant real images matches or outperforms training with targeted images generated from the same upstream data.

papers.title: Towards Calibrated Robust Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper connects shifted-distribution accuracy and calibration through a shared bound and uses it to guide robust fine-tuning.

papers.title: Understanding Bias in Large-Scale Visual Datasets
papers.tldr: The paper analyzes visual attributes, objects, and natural-language descriptions to explain the biases distinguishing large image datasets.

papers.title: Why are Visually-Grounded Language Models Bad at Image Classification?
papers.tldr: The study links weak image classification in vision-language models primarily to training-data exposure and improves performance with classification-focused training.

papers.title: Adaptive Sensitivity Analysis for Robust Augmentation against Natural Corruptions in Image Segmentation
papers.tldr: Faster, lower-storage sensitivity analysis guides adaptive augmentation that improves image segmentation robustness against natural corruptions.

papers.title: Contour Integration Underlies Human-Like Vision
papers.tldr: Controlled fragmentation tests link human-like object recognition to contour integration, a capability that may emerge in models through large-scale training.

papers.title: From Pixels to Perception: Interpretable Predictions via Instance-wise Grouped Feature Selection
papers.tldr: The method makes image predictions more interpretable by selecting meaningful pixel regions and adapting how much information each image retains.

papers.title: LAION-C: An Out-of-Distribution Benchmark for Web-Scale Vision Models
papers.tldr: LAION-C tests web-scale vision models with six new distortions and finds substantial challenges alongside top models matching or exceeding measured human performance.

papers.title: LlavaGuard: An Open VLM-based Framework for Safeguarding Vision Datasets and Models
papers.tldr: LlavaGuard provides openly available vision-language safeguards trained on expert annotations to assess images under customizable safety policies.

papers.title: MaskTwins: Dual-form Complementary Masking for Domain-Adaptive Image Segmentation
papers.tldr: MaskTwins uses theoretically motivated complementary masks to learn domain-invariant segmentation features directly during training.

papers.title: Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.tldr: Orthogonal feature subspaces preserve pretrained visual knowledge while learning fake-image patterns, improving detector generalization.

papers.title: Outlier Gradient Analysis: Efficiently Identifying Detrimental Training Samples for Deep Learning Models
papers.tldr: Outlier gradient analysis connects harmful-sample detection to influence functions while avoiding expensive Hessian calculations.

papers.title: Pixel-level Certified Explanations via Randomized Smoothing
papers.tldr: Randomized smoothing certifies the stability of pixel-level attribution assignments against l2-bounded image perturbations.

papers.title: Stay-Positive: A Case for Ignoring Real Image Features in Fake Image Detection
papers.tldr: Stay-Positive focuses fake-image detectors on generative artifacts, improving generalization, post-processing robustness, and inpainting detection.

papers.title: Targeted Unlearning with Single Layer Unlearning Gradient
papers.tldr: SLUG targets unwanted concepts through a single-layer update, matching reported unlearning performance with substantially less computation.

papers.title: Unveiling AI’s Blind Spots: An Oracle for In-Domain, Out-of-Domain, and Adversarial Errors
papers.tldr: Mentor networks learn to predict another model's errors, with adversarial-error training transferring to other error types and informing SuperMentor.

papers.title: When Dynamic Data Selection Meets Data Augmentation: Achieving Enhanced Training Acceleration
papers.tldr: Jointly choosing training samples and their suitability for augmentation reduces training costs while preserving performance and improving robustness in the reported experiments.

papers.title: You Always Recognize Me (YARM): Robust Texture Synthesis Against Multi-View Corruption
papers.tldr: YARM designs object appearances that improve recognition under image corruption and transfer across tested geometries and model architectures.

papers.title: Approximate Domain Unlearning for Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: The paper introduces a method for selectively reducing a vision-language model’s recognition of specified domains while preserving recognition elsewhere.

papers.title: Automated Detection of Visual Attribute Reliance with a Self-Reflective Agent
papers.tldr: A self-reflective agent improves automated discovery of the visual attributes that influence trained vision models.

papers.title: CaMiT: A Time-Aware Car Model Dataset for Classification and Generation
papers.tldr: CaMiT tracks car models through time and shows benefits from updating recognition models and incorporating temporal information into image generation.

papers.title: ConceptScope: Characterizing Dataset Bias via Disentangled Visual Concepts
papers.tldr: ConceptScope discovers interpretable visual concepts to characterize datasets, detect biases, and organize robustness evaluations.

papers.title: Dataset Distillation for Pre-Trained Self-Supervised Vision Models
papers.tldr: Linear Gradient Matching creates compact synthetic datasets for training classifiers on pretrained vision models, with transfer and interpretability benefits.

papers.title: Dual Data Alignment Makes AI-Generated Image Detector Easier Generalizable
papers.tldr: Dual Data Alignment matches real and synthetic images in pixel and frequency domains to reduce misleading cues and improve detector generalization.

papers.title: Enhancing CLIP Robustness via Cross-Modality Alignment
papers.tldr: COLA improves CLIP's adversarial robustness without training by projecting and realigning image and text representations.

papers.title: Exploring and Leveraging Class Vectors for Classifier Editing
papers.tldr: Class vectors capture class-specific representation changes that can be combined and applied to edit trained image classifiers.

papers.title: FastDINOv2: Frequency Based Curriculum Learning Improves Robustness and Training Speed
papers.tldr: FastDINOv2 reduces pretraining cost through frequency ordering and noise augmentation while matching corruption robustness in the reported configuration.

papers.title: ForensicHub: A Unified Benchmark & Codebase for All-Domain Fake Image Detection and Localization
papers.tldr: ForensicHub unifies datasets, models, and evaluation across four domains of fake-image detection and localization.

papers.title: From Pretraining to Pathology: How Noise Leads to Catastrophic Inheritance in Medical Models
papers.tldr: The paper links inherited pretraining noise to changes in representation statistics and improves medical-model robustness with two lightweight regularizers.

papers.title: ImageNet-trained CNNs are not biased towards texture: Revisiting feature reliance through controlled suppression
papers.tldr: Controlled cue suppression challenges inherent CNN texture bias and reveals feature reliance that varies with architecture, training, and application domain.

papers.title: Learning Robust Vision-Language Models from Natural Latent Spaces
papers.tldr: CoAPT suppresses adversarial image details and restores useful features using pretrained representations, improving the tested balance between robustness and generalization.

papers.title: LORE: Lagrangian-Optimized Robust Embeddings for Visual Encoders
papers.tldr: LORE constrains embedding changes during adversarial fine-tuning to improve visual robustness while largely preserving clean-data accuracy.

papers.title: Mint: A Simple Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models against Common Corruptions
papers.tldr: Mint adapts CLIP during inference by increasing pseudo-label-based separation between classes, improving robustness across tested image corruptions.

papers.title: REOBench: Benchmarking Robustness of Earth Observation Foundation Models
papers.tldr: REOBench finds substantial, task-dependent robustness gaps in Earth observation foundation models across twelve image corruption types.

papers.title: Robust SuperAlignment: Weak-to-Strong Robustness Generalization for Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: An unsupervised weak-to-strong alignment method transfers adversarial robustness through alignment reweighting and refined source guidance.

papers.title: Seeing What Matters: Generalizable AI-generated Video Detection with Forensic-Oriented Augmentation
papers.tldr: Wavelet-based training augmentation helps synthetic-video detectors learn forensic cues that transfer across generators.

papers.title: Spot the Fake: Large Multimodal Model-Based Synthetic Image Detection with Artifact Explanation
papers.tldr: FakeVLM detects synthetic images and explains their artifacts, supported by a dataset of over 100,000 images with natural-language clues.

papers.title: $\texttt{AVROBUSTBENCH}$: Benchmarking the Robustness of Audio-Visual Recognition Models at Test-Time
papers.tldr: AVROBUSTBENCH exposes weaknesses under simultaneous audio-visual corruption, while the proposed AV2C adaptation method substantially improves VGGSOUND-2C performance.

papers.title: Towards Generalizable Detector for Generated Image
papers.tldr: Learning natural-image patterns enables an out-of-distribution approach to generated-image detection with conditional generalization guarantees.

papers.title: Towards Syn-to-Real IQA: A Novel Perspective on Reshaping Synthetic Data Distributions
papers.tldr: SynDR-IQA improves synthetic-data generalization for image quality assessment by increasing content diversity and reducing redundant clusters.

papers.title: Training-free Detection of AI-generated images via Cropping Robustness
papers.tldr: WaRPAD detects generated images without detector training by measuring pretrained representations’ sensitivity to high-frequency perturbations across image patches.

papers.title: TRoVe: Discovering Error-Inducing Static Feature Biases in Temporal Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: TRoVe identifies static visual shortcuts behind temporal-model errors and demonstrates that discovering these biases can help improve test-time performance.

papers.title: Understanding and Enhancing Mask-Based Pretraining towards Universal Representations
papers.tldr: A linear-regression theory of masked pretraining motivates R²MAE, which improves representation learning across evaluated vision, language, and biological models.

papers.title: UniMRSeg: Unified Modality-Relax Segmentation via Hierarchical Self-Supervised Compensation
papers.tldr: UniMRSeg compensates for missing modalities at multiple representation levels so one segmentation network can handle varied input combinations.

papers.title: VLMs can Aggregate Scattered Training Patches
papers.tldr: Vision-language models can combine scattered training patches through shared descriptions, enabling harmful associations to survive sample-level moderation.

papers.title: Beyond Magnitude: Scale-Invariant Evidential Fusion for Multi-View Classification
papers.tldr: SAEF standardizes evidence before combining views, preventing inflated score magnitudes from dominating classification.

papers.title: BiRQA: Bidirectional Robust Quality Assessment for Images
papers.tldr: BiRQA combines bidirectional multiscale features and anchored adversarial training to deliver fast, accurate, and more attack-resistant image quality assessment.

papers.title: BPL: Generalizable Deepfake Detection via Bias-only Pair-aware Learning
papers.tldr: BPL combines comparisons of related real–fake image pairs with bias-only fine-tuning to improve detection of unfamiliar synthetic patterns.

papers.title: Can We Build a Monolithic Model for Fake Image Detection? SICA: Semantic-Induced Constrained Adaptation for Unified-Yet-Discriminative Artifact Feature Space Reconstruction
papers.tldr: SICA uses semantic structure to help one fake-image detector preserve distinct artifact features across four forensic subdomains.

papers.title: DAVE: Distribution-Aware Attribution via ViT Gradient Decomposition
papers.tldr: DAVE decomposes Vision Transformer gradients to produce more stable and detailed attribution maps with stronger reported explanation quality.

papers.title: Dissect and Prune: Enhancing Robustness in AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.tldr: DEAR prunes detector features identified through inpainted images, improving robustness to unseen generators and image post-processing.

papers.title: Divide and Conquer: Reliable Multi-View Evidential Learning for Deepfake Detection
papers.tldr: DiCoME separates semantic and artifact evidence, then models their disagreement to improve deepfake detection and uncertainty estimates.

papers.title: DNA: Uncovering Universal Latent Forgery Knowledge
papers.tldr: DNA isolates forgery-sensitive units already present in pretrained models and reports strong detection with limited examples and unseen generators.

papers.title: Dual-branch Robust Unlearnable Examples
papers.tldr: DUNE combines spatial and color perturbations with model ensembling to make unlearnable examples more robust against training defenses.

papers.title: Feature Collapse Under Corruption: An Entropy Perspective on Robust Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Dem-HEC uses entropy-guided fine-tuning to improve natural-corruption robustness while retaining or improving clean accuracy.

papers.title: FiSeR: Fine-Grained Source Representations for Cross-Domain AI Image Detection
papers.tldr: FiSeR improves cross-domain synthetic-image detection by learning both real-versus-generated distinctions and differences among image generators.

papers.title: Fleet: Few Shots Lead Effective AI-generated Image Detection
papers.tldr: Fleet adapts AI-image detection through constrained routing updates, substantially improving reported performance on a new generator with ten examples.

papers.title: GenShield: Unified Detection and Artifact Correction for AI-Generated Images
papers.tldr: GenShield combines explainable detection of AI-generated images with iterative, controllable correction of their visible artifacts.

papers.title: Geometric Collapse: When Vision Models Fail to Verify Physical Causality
papers.tldr: Controlled edge corruptions reveal that tested depth predictors can spread physically unsupported visual evidence into widespread geometric errors.

papers.title: Geometrically Constrained Outlier Synthesis
papers.tldr: GCOS uses feature-space geometry to synthesize useful training outliers and improves detection of unfamiliar inputs from related semantic domains.

papers.title: Less Precise Can Be More Reliable: A Systematic Evaluation of Quantization’s Impact on VLMs Beyond Accuracy
papers.tldr: Quantization can improve several vision-language reliability measures through spectral filtering, although the reported benefits exclude covariate shift and spurious correlations.

papers.title: MODEL SOUPS NEED ONLY ONE INGREDIENT
papers.tldr: MonoSoup reweights a single model’s fine-tuning updates to retain adaptation gains while improving robustness under distribution shifts.

papers.title: OmniAID: Decoupling Semantics and Artifacts for Universal AI-Generated Image Detection in the Wild
papers.tldr: OmniAID separates content-specific flaws from content-independent artifacts to improve generated-image detection across diverse content and generators.

papers.title: PerceptionRubrics: Calibrating Multimodal Evaluation to Human Perception
papers.tldr: PerceptionRubrics uses image-specific factual checks and gated penalties to expose perceptual failures that broad benchmark scores can conceal.

papers.title: RA-Det: Towards Universal Detection of AI-Generated Images via Robustness Asymmetry
papers.tldr: RA-Det detects generated images through their greater semantic feature drift under controlled perturbations, with reported transfer to unseen generators.

papers.title: Real Data Lies: Unveiling and Closing the Quality Shortcut in Generalizable AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.tldr: Matching and broadening real and synthetic video quality reduces a misleading detection shortcut and improves generalization across real-video quality levels.

papers.title: Remove the Ambiguity: Few-shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection Using Crossmodal Feature Replacer
papers.tldr: CFR selectively replaces unreliable crossmodal reconstructions with confident normal features, improving few-shot anomaly detection when 3D-to-RGB mappings are ambiguous.

papers.title: Robust-U1: Can MLLMs Self-Recover Corrupted Visual Content for Robust Understanding?
papers.tldr: Robust-U1 trains multimodal models to reconstruct corrupted images and reason over both original and recovered inputs, improving robustness in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Robust Vision-Language Models via Manifold-Adversarial Adapters
papers.tldr: Manifold-Adversarial Adapters improve corrupted-image robustness by steering features toward clean-data representations that support multimodal reasoning.

papers.title: Robustifying Vision-Language Models via Test-Time Prompt Adaptation
papers.tldr: RITA improves adversarial robustness by aligning distributions of augmented visual features with text during test-time prompt adaptation.

papers.title: SCalDA: Semantics-Calibrated and Diffusion-Enhanced Data Augmentation
papers.tldr: SCalDA coordinates image, label, and feature semantics during diffusion-enhanced augmentation to improve classification performance.

papers.title: ScoreMix: Synthetic Data Generation by Score Composition in Diffusion Models Improves Recognition
papers.tldr: ScoreMix mixes diffusion scores to create self-contained augmentations, improving face recognition by up to seven percentage points.

papers.title: Segment Anything with Robust Uncertainty-Accuracy Correlation
papers.tldr: RUAC improves SAM’s segmentation and pixel-level uncertainty under joint appearance and shape shifts.

papers.title: Semantic Robustness Certification for Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: The framework uses text-defined semantic transformations to certify ranges of change over which a vision-language model’s predicted class stays fixed.

papers.title: Suppress and Diversify: Refining Robust Pathways for Corruption Robustness
papers.tldr: Suppress and Diversify improves corruption robustness by selecting and diversifying robust computational pathways without extra parameters or test-time overhead.

papers.title: Target-Agnostic Calibration under Distribution Shift with Frequency-Aware Gradient Rectification
papers.tldr: FGR combines frequency filtering with constrained gradient updates to improve calibration under distribution shifts without target-domain access.

papers.title: Unlocking Noise-Resistant Vision: Key Architectural Secrets for Robust Models Against Gaussian Noise
papers.tldr: A large empirical study and theoretical analysis identify architecture and preprocessing choices that improve vision-model robustness to Gaussian noise.

papers.title: VLM-RobustBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Robustness of Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: VLM-RobustBench finds that mild spatial distortions can damage vision-language model performance more than visually severe image corruptions.

papers.title: When Random Saliency Looks Trained: Architectural Center Bias in CNN Interpretability
papers.tldr: Convolutional design choices can create center-focused saliency before training, confounding comparisons between trained and randomized networks.
